items.headline: Malaysian man jailed over 'SMS blaster' phishing scam in Singapore
items.summary: A 28-year-old Malaysian was sentenced to one year and nine months' jail and fined S$1,500 for driving around Singapore with an 'SMS blaster' that pushed phishing texts to nearby phones.

items.headline: Alleged scam-syndicate mastermind handed to Singapore police
items.summary: A 27-year-old Malaysian arrested in Malaysia on Sep 22 was handed to Singapore police the same day, accused of laundering at least S$500,000 in scam proceeds.

items.headline: 52 Singaporeans detained in China over suspected pyramid scheme
items.summary: 52 Singaporeans were arrested and detained in China over suspected pyramid-scheme activities and related offences; Singapore authorities are rendering consular assistance.

items.headline: Leong Sze Hian forfeits S$45,000 after Lim Tean absconds
items.summary: Blogger Leong Sze Hian, 72, forfeited the S$45,000 he put up as bailor after former lawyer Lim Tean allegedly absconded to Malaysia.

items.headline: Ex-HDB director charged with accessing housing database 161 times
items.summary: Tan Chew Ling, 58, a former HDB group director, was charged with accessing the board's housing database 161 times without authorisation under the Computer Misuse Act and Official Secrets Act.

items.headline: India coverage is unavailable in today's edition
items.summary: India's primary outlets were unreachable from the routine's network, and the fallback tier did not surface a verifiable India-domestic story with a working link inside the window.

items.headline: Burnham stands by warning that the UK is 'in hock' to bond markets
items.summary: PM Andy Burnham doubled down on comments that Britain has left itself 'overexposed' to global bond markets, as rising borrowing costs squeeze his government before its first budget.

items.headline: Chancellor Healey must find £10bn to steady UK finances before Oct 28 budget
items.summary: Economists estimate Chancellor John Healey needs about £10 billion in spending cuts or tax rises to stabilise the public finances, with Burnham signalling a 'challenging' budget on 28 October.

items.headline: UK inflation climbs to 3.1% in August, a five-month high
items.summary: Consumer prices rose 3.1% in the year to August, up from 2.9% and the highest since March, as fuel costs climbed, pressuring the Bank of England ahead of its rate decision.

items.headline: Burnham to meet Trump as UK aides blame Washington for economic strain
items.summary: Burnham is set to meet Donald Trump at the UN, with British officials privately blaming the president's policies for higher energy prices and borrowing costs weighing on the UK.

items.headline: Trump welcomes Xi to Washington for first US state visit in a decade
items.summary: Xi Jinping arrived in Washington for a three-day state visit, greeted planeside by Trump at Joint Base Andrews. The main White House meeting Thursday is set to focus on trade, AI, rare earths and the US-Iran war.

items.headline: Macron calls Gaza 'peace' a spectacle that shames the world at the UN
items.summary: In his final UN address, Emmanuel Macron said the so-called peace in Gaza is 'a spectacle that shames us all,' noting no humanitarian corridor had opened. France, Canada and the UK pressed for Palestinian statehood.

items.headline: Iran's Pezeshkian defies Trump in a wartime address to the UN
items.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian held up photos of children he said were killed by US and Israeli bombs, rejected limits on Iran's nuclear program, and said Tehran is ready for diplomacy but not 'the language of force.'

items.headline: Update: Zelensky says Ukraine is ready for an energy ceasefire with Russia
items.summary: Zelensky told the UN Kyiv is ready for an energy ceasefire in any format after meeting Trump, and said Ukraine handed two North Korean soldiers captured fighting for Russia to South Korea.

items.headline: Qualcomm unveils two 2nm smartphone chips built for on-device AI
items.summary: Qualcomm launched the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and a higher-tier Extreme variant, its first 2-nanometer smartphone processors, pushing more agentic AI onto the device rather than the cloud.

items.headline: OpenAI to let outside groups vet its models earlier for safety
items.summary: OpenAI said it will allow third-party organisations to run technical safety assessments during training, evaluation and deployment, naming four priority areas after a summer sandbox-escape incident.

items.headline: Wall Street sells off as Treasury yields jump
items.summary: The S&P 500 fell 0.75% to 7,706.03, the Nasdaq dropped 1.13% to 26,936.04 and the Dow lost 352 points as surging bond yields and rate-hike fears hit equities.

items.headline: US 10-year Treasury yield hits 5.13%, its highest since 2007
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield climbed to about 5.135%, its highest since 2007, as investors bet the Federal Reserve may resume rate hikes amid rising energy costs.

items.headline: Brent crude tops $101 as Middle East tensions lift oil
items.summary: Brent crude rose above $101 a barrel, with the US-Iran war and supply worries pushing energy prices higher and feeding expectations of further Fed tightening.

items.headline: Bets on an October Fed rate hike climb toward 70%
items.summary: Traders raised the odds of another Fed rate increase in October to about 70% after Governor Michael Barr signalled that further tightening may be needed to bring inflation to target.

items.headline: 🏎️ Red Bull confirms Hadjar alongside Verstappen for 2027
items.summary: Red Bull confirmed Isack Hadjar for 2027, locking in its line-up with Max Verstappen, as Formula 1 opened the Azerbaijan Grand Prix weekend in Baku.

items.headline: 🏎️ Verstappen eyes a record third Baku win as F1 runs a rare Saturday race
items.summary: Max Verstappen aims to become the first three-time winner of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, where two-time Baku winner Sergio Perez returns with Cadillac. The race runs Saturday, Sep 26.

items.headline: 🏎️ Ocon declares himself a free agent as Camara leads race for his Haas seat
items.summary: Esteban Ocon said he is a free agent for 2027, with Ferrari junior Rafael Camara emerging as favourite to take his Haas seat, sharpening F1's driver-market intrigue.

items.headline: 🏏 Asian Games men's cricket opens in Japan
items.summary: The men's cricket tournament at the 2026 Asian Games began in Nisshin, Japan, with six lower-seeded teams; Japan met Afghanistan and Hong Kong played Malaysia on the opening day.

items.headline: New Horizons finds signs of recent liquid nitrogen flow on Pluto
items.summary: NASA's New Horizons data suggests liquid nitrogen recently welled up through cracks in Pluto's Sputnik Planitia glacier, the first evidence of recently flowing liquid on the dwarf planet.

items.headline: Telescope spotted a small asteroid just hours before it hit Earth
items.summary: Asteroid 2026 RW1, about 80 cm across, was detected by the Catalina Sky Survey hours before it burned up over the Indian Ocean, only the 13th asteroid spotted before impact.

fun_fact.headline: A shuffled deck of cards is almost certainly a first in history
fun_fact.body: Shuffle a standard 52-card deck and you almost certainly create an ordering that has never existed before. The number of possible arrangements is 52 factorial, about 8x10^67, so vast that no two well-shuffled decks in history have ever matched.

puzzle.title: Who Ate the Cake?
puzzle.body: One of four children (Ann, Ben, Cara, Dan) ate the cake. Exactly one statement is true. Ann: Ben ate it. Ben: Cara ate it. Cara: Ben is lying. Dan: I didn't eat it. Who ate the cake?
puzzle.approach: Ben and Cara contradict each other, so the lone true statement is one of theirs; Ann and Dan both lie.
puzzle.answer: Dan ate the cake. Cara is the sole truth-teller; Dan's lie ('I didn't eat it') makes him the culprit, and it is the only self-consistent solution.

word_puzzle.title: Four by Four
word_puzzle.body: Sort 16 words into 4 groups of 4: KING, SPOT, POLAR, SWORD, SUN, QUEEN, FLASH, JELLY, BROWN, BISHOP, LIME, CAT, KNIGHT, HIGH, SLOTH, STAR.
word_puzzle.approach: Each word joins a compound or a category; resolve the trap words (SUN, KNIGHT, STAR, KING) last.
word_puzzle.answer: ___LIGHT: SPOT, FLASH, LIME, HIGH. Types of bear: POLAR, BROWN, SLOTH, SUN. Chess pieces: KING, QUEEN, BISHOP, KNIGHT. ___FISH: SWORD, JELLY, CAT, STAR.
